trigger_signals: An AI agent is about to be given actions and someone must define which rights it has, who can interrupt it and when rights grow or are revoked
Autonomy for an AI task is being discussed as one label and needs to be split into observe, recommend, draft, simulate and execute rights
guidance: Express graduation as versioned rungs (v1, v2, v3). Each rung names its agency level, the control that bounds it, the evidence threshold to reach it, the data it collects, and the trigger that revokes it.
Every right needs preconditions, scope, rate or spend bounds, confirmation, interruption, rollback or containment, and a fallback when the agent cannot act.
Discriminator: owns the autonomy level, approval points and override paths of an agent; model and data choices come from ai-model-and-data-architecture.

trigger_signals: An approved AI capability needs its model, prompt, retrieval and data design, including whether AI is needed at all
Someone asks whether to use prompting, RAG, fine-tuning or tools, and what data rights, freshness and evaluation that choice needs
ai-model-and-data-architecture.responsibility: Classify an approved AI opportunity's capability needs with a non-AI fallback, then design a bounded model, prompt, retrieval, data-rights, freshness, routing, cost, and evaluation architecture for it.
inputs: An approved AI opportunity or task, data sources, latency and cost constraints, model options, and quality targets.
guidance: Technique decision table: prompting or role instructions when the gap is instructions; RAG when the model needs live, private or changing context it was not trained on (an open-book test); fine-tuning when behavior or style must be consistently specialized; tools when a deterministic system of record must be called. Choose on dynamic context versus behavior specialization.
Classify capability needs across deterministic logic, generation, retrieval, prediction, tools, memory, autonomy, interaction and safety, and always state the non-AI fallback.

Questions this design does not own stay with their specialists: action rights to ai-agent-autonomy-and-human-control, interaction states to ai-interaction-and-probabilistic-ux, abuse and injection risk to ai-safety-and-action-governance. List each as a handoff rather than deciding it here.

Discriminator: owns which model, data and capability design an AI feature uses, including which steps may act autonomously; it does not set the human-control model, the safety policy or the interaction design.

procedure_insert.text: Classify the capability needs and state the non-AI fallback; list unresolved agency, interaction and safety questions as named specialist handoffs.

trigger_signals: An AI feature with tools, data access or actions needs its injection, exfiltration and tool-abuse risks assessed independently
Someone asks what red-team cases, default-deny boundaries and stop conditions an agent needs before release
guidance: Prompt injection cannot be fully solved. Report injection residual risk as non-zero in every assessment; controls reduce impact and likelihood, they never eliminate the risk. Red-team with creative personas and scenarios.
Discriminator: owns misuse, action-risk and governance rules for AI actions; it sets limits that the other AI Skills must respect.

trigger_signals: Several architecture candidates already exist and must be compared on the same criteria with a ranking and a bounded recommendation
A decision maker needs candidate cards, a sensitivity view and diagrams before choosing an architecture
guidance: When criteria and weights are supplied, compute the weighted totals and rank the candidates, showing the arithmetic and a sensitivity check (how the ranking changes if the top weight moves). Withhold a ranking only for criteria that lack evidence, and say which.
Give a conditional recommendation stating what would change it; abstain only when evidence gaps make any ranking misleading.

Choose the diagram pattern per candidate type: a dependency or call-flow graph for coupling, a layered view for boundaries, a sequence view for failure behavior. Vary patterns rather than one template for all candidates.
outputs_add: weighted ranking with arithmetic and sensitivity

procedure_insert.text: Compute weighted totals with the arithmetic shown and rank; mark criteria without evidence instead of scoring them.

trigger_signals: One module needs a smaller, deeper interface that hides complexity with a migration path
Callers know too much about a module and someone must redesign its boundary without rewriting everything
guidance: Testability rules for the challenge step: accept dependencies instead of creating them inside the module, and return results instead of producing side effects, so the interface can be tested without mocking internals.

trigger_signals: A codebase has maintenance friction and someone wants to know which modules are worth deepening and which to leave alone
Repeated orchestration, leaked boundaries or change hotspots must be found with evidence before any redesign
guidance: When the user names no direction, weight areas by recent change frequency (walk back a good stretch of history) before scanning; code that rarely changes rarely pays back a refactor.
If the user named a module or pain point, take it and skip the inference.

trigger_signals: A module interface is being chosen and several structurally different designs should be compared before committing
Someone asks for alternative interface designs with their information hiding, failure behavior and migration cost
guidance: Default to three alternatives, each generated from its own brief so they differ in responsibility boundary or information hiding; use two only when constraints leave room for just two. Renamed signatures over the same boundary do not count.
Include a minimal-change or no-change option when valid, and compare all options on the same declared criteria.

Compare structurally distinct interface alternatives rather than several parameter variants of one facade. Give one provisional recommendation with explicit tradeoffs and what evidence would reverse it.
Recompute every migration total from the supplied categories and show the arithmetic. Keep migratable sites, frozen compatibility sites and total call sites distinct; never relabel their sum.

trigger_signals: A CI workflow runs untrusted pull request code, holds secrets or write tokens, and needs its permissions and triggers hardened
Someone asks which workflow lines let outside input reach a shell, a secret or a privileged job
guidance: Attacker-controllable contexts to trace: issue title and body, pull request title, body, head ref and head branch name, commit messages, and comment bodies. Each must never be interpolated into a shell or script.
Flag pull_request_target combined with a checkout of the pull request head as critical: it runs untrusted code with secrets and a write token.
Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA, not a tag, and set top-level permissions to deny-all or contents: read, granting the minimum per job.

Review the plan from the perspective owned by developer-experience-plan-review

guidance: Scope challenge first: for each sub-problem, cite existing code that already solves it or record that none was found, and name the minimum change that would satisfy the requirement.

trigger_signals: A frontend build may leak server-only code, secrets or privileged logic into the browser bundle
Someone asks whether client and server boundaries, third-party scripts and dependencies are safe before release

anti_add.text: Apply the accepted boundary or dependency repairs to source

frontend-runtime-boundaries-and-dependen.responsibility: Audit authorized frontend source so server-only logic, credentials, privileged actions, assets, dependencies, and runtime assumptions stay on safe explicit boundaries, and hand accepted repairs to the repair owner without editing source.
procedure: Freeze authorized source scope, rendering environments, entry points, dependency graph, bundler behavior, environment variables, assets, browser targets, and existing tests.
Trace client imports, server-only modules, secrets, privileged APIs, dynamic code, third-party scripts, assets, globals, hydration, and environment branches across the build boundary.
Prefer platform or existing dependencies; identify unsafe or unnecessary packages and the server-enforced interface that should hold privileged computation or credentials.
Write each finding with file and line, the boundary crossed, the consequence, and the smallest recommended change, ready for defect-remediation after the owner accepts it.
Define host-run build, bundle, browser, SSR or hydration, and security checks for the repair to pass; report unavailable verification and never expose secret values.

outputs: findings with file, line, boundary crossed and recommended change
artifact_types: findings with file, line, boundary crossed and recommended change

guidance: React Server Components: global state works only in client components; wrap providers in a 'use client' component and keep interactive leaves isolated. A server-only module imported from a client component is a boundary violation.
Audit only. Repairs are a separate accepted action owned by defect-remediation.

trigger_signals: A system needs rules for where secrets live, how they reach runtime and CI, how they rotate and how a leak is handled
A secret may have leaked into logs or a repository and the response order is unclear
guidance: Leak-path examples to map: shell tracing (set -x) in steps that touch secrets, printing environment variables, untrusted multiline data written to the CI environment or output files, secrets passed to steps that run untrusted code or third-party actions, and tokens in request headers that end up in logs.

trigger_signals: A system, repository or pipeline needs an independent threat model and reproducible security findings
Someone asks which attack paths through dependencies, CI, secrets metadata or AI features are real and how severe
guidance: Start with an attack-surface census with counts per category: endpoints, authentication boundaries, external integrations, file upload paths, admin routes, webhooks, background jobs, WebSocket channels, CI workflows, and dependencies. Detect the technology stack first because it changes which checks apply.

Treat the dependency and supply chain as a primary surface: check that third-party CI actions are pinned to full commit SHAs rather than mutable tags, and that lockfiles are enforced (for example npm ci).
Report only findings you can reproduce or evidence; mark a confidence level and filter likely false positives before listing.

procedure_insert.text: Build an attack-surface census with counts per category and detect the stack before tracing threats.
